BTI (#1): U.K. stocks closed higher and an executive was reported selling shares; neither headline clearly explains the ranking.
MO (#2): reports of Japan Tobacco possibly acquiring part of Imperial, and a piece on a potential Altria takeover involving Imperial Brands; this may help explain the attention.
AEO (#3): a preview of the Q3 earnings due 12-02, which fits the catalyst and likely some of the attention.
M (#4): Macy's 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade and a Q3 earnings preview; both plausibly explain the attention.
IOT (#5): a fund filing showing State Street cut its stake, and notice of Q3 earnings on December 3; the earnings date is the more relevant of the two.
DG (#6): a value comparison with ROST and a law firm announcing an investor-claims investigation; neither clearly explains the ranking on its own.
DLTR (#7): commentary on the business since the Family Dollar sale and on an earnings beat, which may explain the continued attention.
FLUT (#9): articles on valuation, tax hits and a paused buyback; they give context but do not clearly explain today's rank.

BTI is #1 (score 0.928) because its 24h move of +3.8% is 2.1 sigmas (momentum percentile 99) and attention (97) and attention on X (98) are far above its own normal, with volume at the 77th percentile and no catalyst listed. MO is #2 (0.904) with the highest attention percentile (100) and attention on X at 99, a 1.2-sigma move (85), but only middling volume (45); its catalyst is a KPI market resolving. AEO is #3 (0.896) on very high volume (98) and strong attention (96) and attention on X (95), with a smaller 0.7-sigma move (65) and earnings on 12-02 as the catalyst.
